concept.name: Active addresses
concept.definition: Active addresses is the count of unique addresses that participated in the network as a sender or receiver in successful transactions over a period — the standard on-chain proxy for network usage and user activity.
concept.intuition: It is the daily foot-traffic count of a blockchain: how many distinct addresses actually showed up and transacted.
concept.mechanics: Analytics providers count unique addresses appearing as input/output of successful transactions per day (or hour); Glassnode's BTC definition counts only addresses active in successful transactions. Trends and divergences from price are the signal — rising activity during a correction, for example, suggests strengthening underlying demand.
concept.failure_modes: One user can control thousands of addresses, so counts overstate unique users; batching, exchange omnibus wallets and L2 migration all distort comparability across time and chains, and address-count heuristics differ between providers.
concept.misconceptions: Active addresses do not equal active users — an exchange can serve millions from a handful of wallets while a coin-mixing user spawns thousands. Raw counts also say nothing about transaction value.
concept.example: Glassnode reports roughly 700,000-750,000 unique BTC addresses active per day in recent readings; a sustained climb from ~2M toward 3M+ on Tron during a price pullback was read as usage diverging positively from price.

citations.source: Glassnode Studio - BTC: Number of Active Addresses
